title: Run, Little Calf
prompt:
A one-minute 3D cartoon comedy from a single brief. On a sunlit slope a little orange calf stands daydreaming when a palm-sized red bird dives past yelling 'Quick — look behind you!'; he turns to find a chopstick-thin white snake stood bolt upright and staring back, screams and bolts, tears through the woods, clears the creek in one leap and runs face-first into a tree. Nursing his nose among the falling leaves he wails; his father — a burly orange-brown bull with long curved horns, slow of speech and long past being surprised by his son — ambles over, hears 'I jumped the creek. I hit the tree,' looks the now-bare tree up and down and wonders aloud whether the tree shouldn't be the one crying. The bird lands at their hooves, the father asks it where the boy's mother has got to, and father and son freeze mid-glance. Bright, saturated cartoon-CG 3D animation, landscape 16:9, native foley throughout, and the brief expressly forbids any lettering drawn into the shots.

The film speaks and subtitles in English, and neither is a setting the brief had to ask for: the deliverable's language is pinned rather than inferred — left to itself the story head reads the spoken language off the setting — and every plan that delivers a film now carries a transcription pass before the composite, so the burned-in captions come from the finished cut rather than from the script. That matters where this was shown: a room loud enough that a film without captions delivers only its picture. An earlier version of this same brief was made in Mandarin, with the subtitles added in a second turn over the already-rendered cut.
